title: A flag declaring arity 1..n swallows the next positional and refuses the repetition its help renders
body:
**A flag declaring `arity: "1..n"` is built greedy-and-once, which inverts BOTH halves of its declared contract: it swallows the positional that follows it, and it refuses the repetition its own help renders.**

`spine.rs`'s flag path gives every non-bool flag `ArgAction::Set`, then applies the declared arity as `num_args(min..)`. For a row declaring `1..n` that composes into "take one or more values, but only once". The help line renders `--kind <kind>...`, which reads as repeatable, and the parser refuses repetition. Meanwhile the greedy value list has no terminator, so the next positional is consumed as another value.

**THE SPELLING THE PROJECT'S OWN CANON PRESCRIBES IS THE BROKEN ONE.** `intent search --kind def <name>` is documented as THE Highlander prior-art check in `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, both of their `lib/templates/llm/` sources, `rules/agnostic/highlander/RULE.md`, and the `in-standards`, `in-plan` and `in-review` skills -- so it reaches every Intent project through the shipped templates, not only this one. It was met by typing it for real while checking prior art for the WP-14 entities.

Driven at `bd79cf605`, literal invocations:

```
intent search --kind def corpus_of      -> error: nothing to search for
intent search corpus_of --kind def      -> ...index/corpus.rs:136  def  -  corpus_of
intent search corpus_of --kind def --kind ref
                                        -> error: the argument '--kind <kind>...' cannot be used multiple times
intent search corpus_of --kind def ref  -> two hits (the undocumented list form is the only one that works)
```

**CONTROL, which is what makes this a class rather than three anecdotes:** `intent search --limit 3 corpus_of` works with the flag first. `--limit` declares no `1..n` arity and keeps `ArgAction::Set`'s exactly-one, so the position of the flag is irrelevant to it. The defect tracks the declaration, not the command.

**SIX FLAGS ACROSS THREE COMMANDS DECLARE `1..n`, and every one of them is affected.** `search --tier/--lang/--kind`, `at new --covers`, `at edit --ac`, `critic --files`. The two `1..n` ARGS (`lang init`, `lang remove`) are positionals built on a different path and are not affected.

The consequence is worse away from `search`, because the swallowed positional is required:

```
intent critic --files <path> rust          -> error: the following required arguments were not provided: <LANG>
intent at new --covers AC-99.9 ST9999 AT-99.9
                                           -> error: the following required arguments were not provided: <STID>, <ATID>
```

Both refuse loudly rather than doing the wrong thing, which is why this has been survivable; `search` is the case that returns a refusal a caller reads as "no such thing" rather than "you held it wrong".

**FIX:** a flag whose declared arity is unbounded becomes append-with-one-value -- `ArgAction::Append` with `num_args(1)` -- so `--kind def --kind ref` repeats as the help already promises and the flag stops eating the positional. **The fix goes in the spine and is read from the declared arity, never special-cased on a flag's name**, for the reason `flag_reachability.rs` already states about hand-listed populations: a seventh instance arriving under another name would be invisible to a check that knows only these six.

**STATED COST:** the undocumented space-separated list form `--kind def ref` stops parsing as two values. Nothing documents it, and it is the same greed that causes the defect.
